newsitem.title: USA: Intel unveils Pentium MMX chip pricing.
newsitem.headline: Intel unveils Pentium MMX chip pricing.

text.p: Intel Corp unveiled Wednesday pricing plans for its much awaited new Pentium processors with multimedia extension (MMX) technology.

The chipmaker said 166- and 200-megahertz MMX Pentium processors for desktop PCs are priced at $407 and $550 per chip in 1,000-unit quantities. These amounts reflect prices computer makers that build the chips into new PCs will pay.

It said 150- and 166-megahertz MMX Pentiums for mobile computer systems are priced at $443 and $550 in 1,000 unit quanties. The mobile chip pricing reflects a premium for lower voltage operation required for notebook computers.
The company said the new MMX processors for both desktop and mobile computers are available immediately.
The new microprocessors are the first to incorporate Intel's MMX technology that provides for improved graphics, video and audio features in PCs using the chips.

Intel said its MMX technology is fully compatible with previous Intel chip designs and with widely used operating systems -- a reference to Microsoft Corp's Windows operating system software -- and other application software.
The technology will be included in future processors, including Pentium OverDrive processors, an upgrade that allows previously manufactured computers to be beefed up with more powerful features.
The first of these processors will be introduced in the first half of this year for upgradeable Pentium processor-based systems, the company said.
The Pentium processors contain 4.5 million transistors.
